chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Yazīd al-Kunāsī, who said:

I asked Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), “Was ʿĪsā ibn Maryam (عليه السلام), when he spoke in the cradle, the hujjah of Allah over the people of his time?” He said, “On that day he was a Prophet, the hujjah of Allah, though not sent as a messenger. Do you not hear his statement when he said:”
“Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Book and made me a Prophet. And He has made me blessed wherever I may be, and has enjoined upon me salat and zakat as long as I remain alive.”

I said, “So on that day, in that state while he was in the cradle, was he a hujjah of Allah over Zakariyyā?” He said, “In that state, ʿĪsā was a sign for the people and a mercy from Allah for Maryam when he spoke and spoke on her behalf. He was a Prophet, a hujjah over those who heard his speech in that condition. Then he became silent and did not speak until two years had passed for him, and Zakariyyā was the hujjah of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, over the people after the silence of ʿĪsā for those two years.”
Then Zakariyyā died, and his son Yaḥyā inherited from him the Book and the wisdom while he was a small child. Do you not hear the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
“O Yaḥyā, hold fast to the Book with strength,” and “We gave him judgment while still a child.”

So when ʿĪsā (عليه السلام) reached seven years of age, he spoke with prophethood and messengership when Allah, the Exalted, revealed to him. Thus ʿĪsā became the hujjah over Yaḥyā and over all the people. And the earth, O Abū Khālid, does not remain even for a single day without a hujjah of Allah over the people, ever since the day Allah created Ādam (عليه السلام) and settled him on the earth.”

So I said, “May I be made your ransom, was ʿAlī (عليه السلام) a hujjah from Allah and His Messenger over this Ummah during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله)?” He said, “Yes—on the day he established him for the people, set him up as a banner, called them to his wilayah, and commanded them to obey him.”

I said, “And was obedience to ʿAlī (عليه السلام) obligatory upon the people during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and after his passing?” He said, “Yes, but he remained silent and did not speak alongside the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله). Obedience to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) was binding upon his Ummah and upon ʿAlī (عليه السلام) during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله). And obedience to ʿAlī (عليه السلام), from Allah and from His Messenger, was binding upon all the people after the passing of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), and ʿAlī (عليه السلام) was wise and knowledgeable.”

ai.seo_question: Was Imam ʿAlī (عليه السلام) Allah’s hujjah during the lifetime of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) and after his death?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that divine proof (ḥujjah) remains continuously on the earth, illustrated through the lives of ʿĪsā, Zakariyyā, and Yaḥyā (عليهم السلام). It then applies this principle to Imam ʿAlī (عليه السلام), affirming his divinely mandated authority and obligatory obedience after the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله).

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Yazeed Al Kunasy who said, 
‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Was Isa<sup>as</sup> Ibn Maryam<sup>as</sup>, when he<sup>as</sup> spoke in the cradle, a Divine Authority of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> upon the people of his<sup>asws</sup> era?’

So heasws said: ‘Heas was a Prophetas in those days, a Divine Authority of Allahazwj without being a Mursil. Have you not listened to hisas words when heas said [19:30] He said: I am a servant of Allah; He has Given me the Book and Made me a Prophet [19:31] And He has Made me Blessed wherever I may be, and He has Enjoined upon me with the Prayer and the Zakat for as long as I live?’.

I said, ‘In those days he<sup>as</sup> was a Divine Authority upon Zakariyya<sup>as</sup> in that state, and he<sup>as</sup> (Isa<sup>as</sup>) was in the cradle?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Isa<sup>as</sup>, in that state, was a Sign for the people and a Mercy from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> to Maryam<sup>as</sup> when he<sup>as</sup> spoke, so he<sup>as</sup> expressed on her<sup>as</sup> behalf, and he<sup>as</sup> was a Prophet<sup>as</sup>, a Divine Authority upon the ones who heard his<sup>as</sup> speech in that state. Then he<sup>as</sup> was silent, so he<sup>as</sup> did not speak until two years passed by for him<sup>as</sup>, and it was so that Zakariyya<sup>as</sup> was the Divine Authority of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic upon the people after the silence of Isa<sup>as</sup> by two years.

Then Zakariyyaas passed away, so hisas sonas Yahyaas inherited himas, the Book and the Wisdom, and heas was a young child. Have you not listened to the Words of the Mighty and Majestic [19:12] O Yahya!
Grab hold of the Book with strength; and We Granted him the Wisdom whilst he was a child?

So when Isa<sup>as</sup> reached the age of seven years, he<sup>as</sup> spoke with the Prophet-hood and the Messenger-ship when Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted Revealed unto him<sup>as</sup>. So Isa<sup>as</sup> was the Divine Authority upon Yahya<sup>as</sup> and upon the people altogether, and the earth doesn’t remain, O Abu Khalid, even for one day without a Divine Authority of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> upon the people since the day Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Created Adam<sup>as</sup> and Settled him<sup>as</sup> in the earth’. 
So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>!

Was Ali<sup>asws</sup> a Divine Authority of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup> upon this community during the lifetime of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, the day he<sup>saww</sup> nominated him<sup>asws</sup> to the people and established him<sup>asws</sup> as a flag and called them to his<sup>as</sup> Wilayah and ordered them with his<sup>asws</sup> obedience’.

I said, ‘And was it so that the obedience to Ali<sup>asws</sup> was an Obligation upon the people during the lifetime of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> and after his<sup>saww</sup> passing away?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, but he<sup>asws</sup> was silent, so he<sup>asws</sup> did not speak along with Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and it was so that the obedience to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was upon his<sup>saww</sup> community and upon Ali<sup>asws</sup> during the lifetime of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and it was so that the obedience for Ali<sup>asws</sup> was from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and from His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup> upon the people, all of them, after the passing away of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and it was so that Ali<sup>asws</sup> was wise, knowledgeable’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from Yazid al-Kunasiyy who has said the following.

“I asked abu Ja‘far (a.s.), ‘Was Jesus at the time he spoke to people from the cradle a Divine authority over the people of his time?” He said, “At that time he was a prophet, a Divine authority over the people but not a Mursal (Messenger).

Have you not heard the words of Allah that say, “He said, “I am the servant of God. He has given me the Book and has appointed me to be a Prophet [19:30]. He has blessed me no matter where I dwell, commanded me to worship Him and pay the religious tax for as long as I live.”

[19:31] I then said, “Was he the Divine authority over Zackaria at the time that he was in the cradle?” He said, “At that time Jesus was a sign from Allah and a blessing to Mary (Maryam) when he spoke on her behalf. He was a prophet and a Divine authority over all those who heard his words at that time. Thereafter he did not speak until he was two years old. At Such time Zackaria was the Divine authority of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most gracious, over the people after the silence of Jesus.

Zackaria then died and his son Yahya (John) inherited the book and wisdom and he was a small child. You can hear it in the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most gracious, “We commanded John, Zachariah’s son), “O John, follow the guidance of the Lord with due steadfastness.
We gave knowledge and wisdom to John during his childhood.”

[19:12] When Jesus became seven years he then spoke as a prophet and a messenger until Allah, the Most Holy sent him inspiration. Thus, Jesus was the Divine authority over John and over all the people. The earth is never left without the presence of a Divine authority over the people, O abu Khalid, from the day Allah created Adam and settled him on earth.”

I then said, May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, “Did Ali (a.s.) possess Divine authority from Allah and His Messenger over this nation (Muslims) during the life time of the Messenger of Allah?”

He said, “Yes, but he kept silent and did not speak along with the Messenger of Allah. At that time, during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah, obedience was of the rights of the Messenger of Allah over the ’Umma (nation) and over Ali (a.s.). Obedience on the authority of Allah and the Messenger of Allah over the people as a whole was obligatory to Ali (a.s.) after the death of the Messenger of Allah. Ali (a.s.) was a very wise and knowledgeable person.”
